# Docked DevTools shifts every cross-window drop zone by half its width

## Context

Reported by @tobiu, 2026-09-09, who also specified the required scope: **right and bottom docks are both in normal use**; left and top are rare. Dragging a native popup back into a Workstation window works correctly — 1.2s dwell, the drop zone fills, the view moves, the popup closes — **unless Chrome DevTools is docked to a side**. Then dragging in from the right makes drop zones activate while the pointer is still over the DevTools panel.

Measured on his own window, docked right, with a one-line console probe:

```
{trueViewportX: 64, modelSaysX: 303.5, devtoolsWidth: 479}
```

`303.5 − 64 = 239.5 = 479 / 2`. The error is exactly half the DevTools width, to the pixel.

## The Problem

`Neo.manager.Window#calculateGeometry` (`src/manager/Window.mjs:74`) derives the viewport origin from the frame origin by splitting the frame/viewport difference across assumed window borders:

```javascript
widthDiff    = outerWidth - innerWidth,
// Assumption: Side borders are symmetric
sideBorder   = widthDiff / 2,
// Assumption: Bottom border matches side border (common in Windows)
bottomBorder = sideBorder,
topChrome    = heightDiff - bottomBorder;
```

Both assumptions describe **OS window borders**. A docked DevTools panel is not a border: it consumes `innerWidth` on **one** side while `outerWidth` is unchanged. The split then invents `widthDiff / 2` of phantom border on each side and subtracts the same amount from the title-bar height.

Run through the real function — a 1600×1000 macOS Chrome frame at (100, 50), with the browser's own 87px of top chrome, and the truth computed independently of the model (viewport = frame top + 87, plus the panel only when the panel is on that edge):

| dock | model origin | true origin | error |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | (100, 137) | (100, 137) | **OK** |
| **right 479** | (339.5, −102.5) | (100, 137) | (+239.5, −239.5) |
| **bottom 400** | (100, 537) | (100, 137) | **(0, +400)** — the whole panel height |
| **left 479** | (339.5, −102.5) | (579, 137) | (−239.5, −239.5) |
| top 400 | (100, 537) | (100, 537) | OK |

The unifying statement, and the reason no case analysis will fix this: **the split is only ever right when the entire frame/viewport difference genuinely sits above the viewport.** That holds with no DevTools and, coincidentally, with a top dock — the code puts all leftover height into `topChrome`, which is correct exactly when the panel really is on top. Every other dock position is wrong.

Three consequences worth stating precisely:

1. **The viewport SIZE is correct in every row.** Only the **origin** is wrong. The fix is a one-place origin correction, not a re-model.
2. **A bottom dock is wrong by the full panel height**, not half. The modeled viewport spans y 537–1050 while the real one spans 137–650 — i.e. the model places the viewport exactly where the DevTools panel is. The reported symptom is the right-dock case only because that is the direction the drag comes from; the bottom case produces the same class of false zone activation along the bottom edge.
3. **Left and right are indistinguishable to the model** — both produce origin (339.5, −102.5) — while their truths differ by the panel width. No clamping scheme can separate them, because the inputs are identical.

## The Architectural Reality

- **The signal already arrives.** `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:1114` `observeWindowGeometry` arms `observeMovement` **and** `observeResize` for the host's own first real window binding and for every admitted vessel (#18077 added the `resize` listener at `src/main/addon/WindowPosition.mjs:126`). Docking DevTools fires `window.resize`, `publishGeometry()` sends a fresh `getWindowData()` snapshot, and `manager.Window#onWindowPositionChange` recomputes. **This is not a detection gap.**
- **Where it manifests:** `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs:1104-1105` computes `localX = screenX - targetWindow.innerRect.x` (same shape at `:897` and `:1008`). A viewport origin 240px too far right maps every screen point 240px too far left in page space, so a pointer physically over DevTools lands on live page content near the right edge.
- **`getWindowAt` is innocent.** `src/manager/Window.mjs:55` hit-tests `outerRect`, which legitimately contains the DevTools strip — it is inside the OS window. The error is purely the page-space mapping.
- **The consumers that read `innerRect` for its size are also innocent:** `DragAffordances#getGeometrySignature` (`:209`) and `Participation#defaultHitTest` (`:457`) use `width`/`height` only, and those are correct.
- **Firefox already takes the exact route.** `calculateGeometry:99` branches on `mozInnerScreenX`, which publishes the viewport origin directly. Chrome has no such property — but it has an exact measurement, below.
- **Predecessor:** #18058 made `screenLeft`/`screenTop` the *frame* origin, which is what made this split load-bearing for hit-tests. That ticket is complete and correct; this is the assumption it left standing, now falsified with a real case. This is an unmasking, not a regression, and carries no `Resolves` for it.

## The Fix

For any pointer event, **`event.screenX - event.clientX` is the viewport's screen-space left origin** and `event.screenY - event.clientY` its top — by definition, with no assumption about borders, dock side, platform, or menu bar. `git grep` confirms nothing in the tree uses this today. A cross-window drag is pointer-driven, so samples are abundant exactly when this matters.

- `src/main/addon/WindowPosition.mjs` measures it. The addon is already in the mouse-event business (`:91` registers `mouseout`). Arm a one-shot `pointermove` listener that records the origin and removes itself; re-arm it from `onResize`, so a DevTools dock/undock/re-dock recalibrates on the next pointer motion. No poll, no permanent listener.
- The measured origin reaches the worker the way native effects already do — a main-thread stash read by `Main#getWindowData` (`src/Main.mjs:326` reads `win.neoNativeGeometryEffects` in exactly this shape).
- `calculateGeometry` prefers the measured origin when present, alongside the existing `mozInnerScreenX` branch, and falls back to today's split when a window has never seen a pointer. Additive: a window with no sample behaves exactly as it does now.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.manager.Window#calculateGeometry` | CSSOM View: `MouseEvent.screenX`/`clientX` | Prefers a measured viewport origin; keeps the Firefox `mozInnerScreenX` branch ahead of it | The current symmetric split, unchanged, when no sample exists | Method docblock states which of the three sources answered | Unit arms over all three source paths, incl. the measured table above |
| `Main#getWindowData` payload (`src/Main.mjs:316`) | Existing `neoNativeGeometryEffects` stash idiom | Adds an optional measured-origin field; absent until a pointer sample lands | Field absent ⇒ consumers see today's payload | JSDoc on the new field | A payload assertion with and without a sample |
| `WindowPosition` (`src/main/addon/WindowPosition.mjs`) | Its existing `mouseout` / `resize` listeners | One-shot pointer calibration, re-armed by `onResize` | `observeResize: false` ⇒ no calibration, as today | Config + method docblocks | A resize re-arms; a second pointer event after calibration adds no listener |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a measured viewport origin present, `calculateGeometry` returns that origin verbatim and derives `chrome` from it. Asserted against **all five rows** of the table in The Problem — including the `topChrome` sign for a side dock and the full-height error for a bottom dock. **Right and bottom are the required cases** (@tobiu, 2026-09-09: both are in normal use); left and top must not regress and fall out of the same measurement for free.
- [ ] With no measured origin, `calculateGeometry` returns byte-identical output to current `dev` for the same input. The regression arm pins the **no-DevTools** row — the only configuration that is correct today for a non-coincidental reason.
- [ ] Firefox's `mozInnerScreenX` branch keeps priority over the measured origin; an arm supplies both and asserts the Firefox value wins.
- [ ] The calibration is one-shot per resize: an arm proves a second pointer event after a sample registers no additional listener, and that `onResize` re-arms it. A permanently attached `pointermove` on every window is a rejected shape.
- [ ] `DragCoordinator`'s screen→local conversion is proven end to end at the model level: given a DevTools-shaped window report, a screen point over the panel maps outside the viewport and `acceptsRemoteDrag` is not consulted. Mutation-proven — reverting the origin preference reddens it.
- [ ] The PR states the browser-zoom bound explicitly and shows what the code does at zoom ≠ 1, rather than leaving it implied.

## Out of Scope

Any change to `getWindowAt` or `outerRect` semantics; #18058's frame-origin decision; the DevTools panel's own size as a reportable quantity (no web API exposes it, and the fix does not need it); the drag dwell timer and drop-zone rendering; the stray `console.log` at `src/manager/Window.mjs:146`, which is a separate defect-note.

## Avoided Traps

Do **not** replace the symmetric assumption with a different assumption. A left dock and a right dock produce byte-identical inputs to `calculateGeometry` (both `outerWidth − innerWidth = 479`), so no clamping, heuristic or side-guess can separate them — the information is not in the payload. Only a measurement carries it. Do not attach a permanent `pointermove` listener on every window. Do not assume `screenX - clientX` is exact under browser page zoom: `clientX` is page CSS px, `screenX` screen CSS px, so the value must be sanity-bounded against the frame rather than trusted blindly. Do not derive the panel width from `outerWidth - innerWidth` and attribute it to a guessed side.

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029` — no engine host, Group, projection or native-window contract changes. `calculateGeometry` gains a preferred input; its output contract is unchanged.
